claims.text: The proposed intervention combines machine learning with first-principles calculations.
The intervention applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in high-temperature solid states.
The intervention applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in liquid states.
Machine learning and first-principles calculations can overcome current limitations in accuracy, availability, and efficiency across a large compositional space.
The intervention can accurately predict melting temperature.
The intervention can accurately predict enthalpy of fusion.
The intervention can accurately predict entropy of fusion.
The intervention can accurately predict volume change upon melting.
The intervention can accurately predict liquid thermodynamic properties.
Lattice distortion is a structural mediator relevant to predicting the stated thermodynamic properties.
Compositional fluctuations are a structural mediator relevant to predicting the stated thermodynamic properties.
Accounting for lattice distortion and compositional fluctuations causes the computational models to predict thermodynamic properties accurately.
Lattice distortion and compositional fluctuations are difficult to capture using traditional experimental methods.
The intervention will improve accuracy relative to traditional experimental methods such as differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction.
The intervention will improve efficiency in determining the listed thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality of the training data.
Model accuracy may depend on alloy-system complexity.
The proposed validation compares computational predictions with experimental measurements for a range of high-entropy alloys.
A significant deviation between predictions and experimental data would falsify the hypothesis.
